data.title: Citi Predicts Up to 410% Rally for These 2 'Strong Buy' Stocks
data.description:
With the third quarter well underway and most second-quarter earnings now in the rearview mirror, investors are starting to look ahead to the rest of 2026 and how best to position their portfolios.

The good news is that the latest earnings season has given investors plenty to work with. According to FactSet, S&P 500 earnings are on track to rise about 50% year-over-year in the second quarter, which would mark the index's strongest earnings growth since Q2 2021. Meanwhile, profit margins are on track to reach nearly 17%, their highest level in more than 15 years.

And the strength could have staying power. If current estimates hold, 2026 would mark the third consecutive year of double-digit earnings growth for the S&P 500, something the market has not seen in two decades. That gives investors a strong fundamental backdrop heading into the remainder of the year.

Citi strategist Scott Chronert believes the next phase of the market's run could become less concentrated, with gains continuing to broaden beyond the stocks that have done much of the heavy lifting.

"With Q2 earnings mostly behind us, we lift our full year S&P 500 index estimate to $365 from a previous $350. The fundamental tailwinds supporting our year-end 8100 target remain mostly in place. Broadening has been happening and should continue premised on our expectation for the market to price out Fed rate hikes," Chronert noted.

While Citi sees more room for the broader market to rise, some individual stocks could have far greater upside. In fact, the firm's 5-star analyst, Yigal Nochomovitz, sees triple-digit gains ahead for two names, with one offering potential upside of as much as 410%.

After running the tickers through TipRanks' database, we found out that each has been scoring points with the rest of the Street, earning a "Strong Buy" consensus rating. Let's take a closer look.

Biomea Fusion (BMEA)

We'll start with Biomea Fusion, the first of Citi's picks. The clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company is developing new treatments for diabetes and obesity, two widespread conditions linked to a broad range of serious health complications and premature death. With demand for new and more effective therapies remaining high, success in either market could open a significant commercial opportunity for the company.

Biomea has two drug candidates in the pipeline right now: Icovamenib, a potential first-in-class therapeutic agent designed to restore beta-cell function in diabetes, and BMF-650, a small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist designed for oral dosing and currently under investigation as a treatment for obesity and type-2 diabetes.

Starting with the more advanced Icovamenib program, earlier results have provided some encouragement. In the Phase II COVALENT-111 study, patients with Type 2 diabetes who remained inadequately controlled while receiving GLP-1-based therapy saw a mean 1.2-percentage-point reduction in HbA1c at Week 52, a statistically significant improvement versus placebo. Importantly, that improvement was sustained through Week 52, months after treatment with icovamenib had ended. The subgroup also showed improvements in C-peptide index, supporting the drug's potential to improve the body's own insulin secretion. Icovamenib was generally well tolerated, with no treatment-related serious adverse events or treatment discontinuations due to adverse events reported in the analysis.

Biomea is now building on those results through several ongoing studies. COVALENT-211 and COVALENT-212 are evaluating Icovamenib in different groups of patients with Type 2 diabetes, with data on their 26-week primary endpoints expected in 1Q27 and 2Q27, respectively. On the obesity side, Biomea has dosed the first patient in the OPAL study, which will evaluate 12 weeks of icovamenib in combination with 24 weeks of low-dose semaglutide against 24 weeks of low-dose semaglutide alone. The study is enrolling people without Type 2 diabetes who are either overweight or obese.

The nearer-term catalyst for Biomea shares, however, comes from BMF-650, which is currently in a Phase I trial. Earlier this summer, Biomea expanded the ongoing study to test faster dose escalation and the potential for greater weight loss with BMF-650. The completed cohorts have so far produced a favorable safety and tolerability profile, with no dose-limiting toxicities observed. Investors won't have to wait long for the next update, as Biomea expects to release data on the initial 28-day clinical weight reduction experience during this quarter.

With BMEA currently trading at just $1.37, Citi's Yigal Nochomovitz believes now is the time to snap up shares ahead of the upcoming catalyst.

"We expect increased investor interest in the company's internally developed oral GLP-1 candidate (BMF-650) when management announces 28-day weight reduction data in healthy overweight or obese volunteers from the Ph1 GLP-131 study in 3Q26. We believe BMF-650 represents an interesting opportunity worth pursuing as a potentially safer, but equally effective, oral GLP-1 compared to existing therapies in this category. BMF-650 was designed based on the chemotype of orforglipron, LLY's oral GLP-1, but with slightly lower potency to possibly improve tolerability and a shallower peak-to-trough ratio to enhance PK properties. We are encouraged by preclinical data where BMF-650 has demonstrated seemingly 2-3x greater oral availability than orforglipron, and where BMF-650 has shown up to ~15% weight loss in NHPs after 28 days of treatment," Nochomovitz noted.

Based on BMF-650's potential and the strength of Biomea's broader pipeline, Nochomovitz rates BMEA shares a Buy with a $7 price target. That figure reflects his confidence in BMEA's ability to soar 410% over the next twelve months. (To watch Nochomovitz's track record, click here)

Citi isn't the only bull when it comes to BMEA shares. The Wall Street consensus here is a Strong Buy, based on 5 unanimous Buy ratings. The average price target of $6.80 is nearly as bullish as Citi's, implying about 396% upside over the next 12 months. (See BMEA stock forecast)

data.title: Market Wrap: U.S. Stocks Post Losing Week Despite Friday Rally
data.description:
U.S. stocks posted a strong rally on Aug. 21, ending the trading week on a positive note. The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average finished trading at 53,277, up 517 points or 0.98% on the day. The benchmark S&P 500 index was up 33.21 points or 0.43%. And the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite (NDAQ) index was up 113 points or 0.44%.

However, the Friday rally couldn't prevent stocks from posting a weekly loss after several bruising days for the U.S. market. The S&P 500 snapped a three-week winning streak as it declined a little more than 1%. The Nasdaq finished the week 2% lower and ended a three-week win streak, while the Dow fell nearly 1% on the week and posted back-to-back weekly losses.

Rising Treasury Yields

Rising Treasury yields and crude oil prices pressured stocks earlier in the week. The Friday market rally occurred despite both government bond yields and crude oil prices continuing to march higher. Yields keep ticking upwards even after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he would double repurchases of U.S. government bonds in coming months to $4 billion or more.

In terms of bright spots in the market, cryptocurrencies rallied hard in recent days, with Bitcoin (BTC) and other digital assets moving sharply higher. After stagnating for months, Bitcoin's price has risen more than 20% in the last two days and was near $77,000 heading into the weekend. Crypto got a shot in the arm after U.S. President Donald Trump called on Congress to pass the Clarity Act legislation that will provide a regulatory roadmap for digital assets.

Below is a list of the top trending U.S. stocks on Aug. 21. As one can see in the chart, the majority of stocks are retailers such as Walmart (WMT) and Home Depot (HD). This is likely because the major American retailers reported their earnings for this year's second quarter over the past week, as did technology company Analog Devices (ADI).

data.title: Applied Optoelectronics Stock Is Plunging After Hours — What Spooked Investors and What Wall Street Sees Next
data.description:
Applied Optoelectronics (NASDAQ:AAOI) stock is plunging about 10% in after-hours trading Friday after the optical-networking company unveiled another $600 million at-the-market stock offering. The announcement appears to have spooked investors over further dilution, especially after AAOI spent much of 2026 raising capital through similar programs. Under the new agreement with Raymond James and Needham, the company can sell up to $600 million of common stock from time to time at prevailing market prices.

Summer Sale - Claim 70% Off TipRanks

AAOX: an alternative to margin or options on AAOI

Applied Optoelectronics had raised about $1.05 billion in gross proceeds through ATM offerings by the end of June, selling close to 7.8 million shares along the way. Those transactions included a $500 million program completed in April, followed by sales through another $600 million facility launched during May. Friday's filing therefore opens the door to another sizable round of stock issuance after investors have absorbed substantial dilution this year.

Yet, AAOI has been putting that capital toward a period of rapid expansion. Earlier this year, the company announced plans to expand its Pearland, Texas, manufacturing footprint by nearly 400,000 square feet as it works to increase production of 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers used in AI infrastructure. Management expects demand for those high-speed products to remain above available production capacity through the middle of 2027.

Recent financial results show how fast the company has been growing alongside that expansion. Second-quarter revenue climbed 86% year-over-year to a record $191.9 million, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of record sales. The company returned to non-GAAP profitability with earnings of $0.06 per share, while 800G product volumes more than doubled sequentially during the period.

Management expects another sizable increase during the third quarter as production continues expanding. The company guided for revenue between $255 million and $290 million, alongside non-GAAP earnings ranging from $0.11 to $0.26 per share. AAOI is working toward manufacturing capacity of around 650,000 800G and 1.6T units per month by year-end, compared with capacity approaching 200,000 units monthly when second-quarter results were released.

Investors are now balancing AAOI's strong operating momentum against the dilution risk that comes with funding its rapid expansion. Demand for high-speed optical products remains robust, while sales and manufacturing capacity continue climbing. For now, Friday's after-hours plunge suggests investors are focusing more on the potential cost of that growth.

Overall, Wall Street leans bullish on AAOI, although analysts differ on where the stock goes from here. AAOI earns a Moderate Buy consensus rating, with 3 analysts saying Buy and 2 remaining sidelined. The average 12-month price target stands at $163.40, representing about 31% upside from Friday's closing price. (See AAOI stock forecast)

data.title: Top Oppenheimer Analyst Sets the Stage on Nvidia Stock Ahead of Earnings
data.description:
All eyes will be on Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) Wednesday, August 26, when the AI giant delivers one of the most anticipated earnings reports of the season. With Wall Street expecting another quarter of explosive growth, investors will be looking for the kind of performance that can remind them why Nvidia became one of the market's biggest winners.

And those memories set a very high bar. Nvidia stock is up about 16% year-to-date, a gain most companies would gladly take, but one that looks modest compared with Nvidia's history. At roughly the same point in 2025, shares had climbed about 30%, while in 2024 they had soared close to 160%. Investors hoping Wednesday's report can bring back some of that magic should keep one thing in mind: delivering those kinds of returns becomes much harder when you are worth $5.2 trillion.

Still, Nvidia continues to grow at a pace rarely seen from a company of its size. Wall Street expects the chipmaker to report record fiscal second-quarter revenue of about $92 billion, nearly double the year-ago level, with Data Center revenue once again accounting for the majority of sales.

One analyst setting the stage for Nvidia ahead of the report is Oppenheimer's Rick Schafer. The 5-star analyst, who ranks #22 among more than 10,000 Wall Street analysts tracked by TipRanks, rates NVDA shares Outperform (i.e., Buy) alongside a $265 price target, which implies about 23% upside for the next 12 months. (To watch Schafer's track record, click here)

Schafer expects the rollout of Nvidia's next-generation VR200 systems, which are on track to ramp in the current quarter, to strengthen second-half growth. The analyst projects more than $1 trillion in combined revenue from GB200, GB300 and VR200 between 2025 and 2027, while Nvidia's annual accelerator upgrade cycle should help preserve its technological advantage.

That product roadmap is one reason Schafer calls Nvidia the "undisputed AI infrastructure leader." His confidence extends beyond GPUs, with the company offering processors, networking equipment, interconnect technology and CUDA software as part of an end-to-end computing platform. The analyst expects Data Center revenue to rise 15% sequentially, while Networking revenue is projected to increase 35%.

China could provide another boost. Schafer believes sales of Nvidia's H200 accelerator there could "provide added upside optionality (>$50B)." Such a contribution would give Nvidia another sizable revenue opportunity beyond the growth the analyst expects from Blackwell Ultra and the upcoming Vera Rubin generation.

And despite Nvidia's enormous valuation, Schafer does not think the opportunity has run its course. "We remain long-term buyers," he said. The analyst models $212 billion in free cash flow this year and $312 billion next year, leaving Nvidia with substantial financial capacity for share repurchases, supply-chain investments and expansion throughout its AI ecosystem.

Schafer sums up Nvidia's competitive position with perhaps his strongest description: "AI's castle on the hill."

The rest of the Street sees even more upside ahead. In fact, Wall Street is unanimous on Nvidia, with all 26 analysts covering the stock over the past three months recommending a Buy, giving NVDA a Strong Buy consensus rating. The average price target of $301.82 points to about 41% upside from current levels. (See NVDA stock forecast)

data.title: Boeing (BA) Union Rejects Contract, Setting Stage for Potential Strike
data.description:
Boeing's (BA) biggest white-collar union, the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace (SPEEA), voted to reject the company's four‑year contract offer and gave clear approval to its negotiating team to call a strike if a new deal cannot be reached, Reuters reported.

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

The vote covered about 17,000 Boeing workers across two key groups. In the Professional Unit, which includes 13,000 engineers and scientists, 64.3% voted to reject the offer, and 87.8% backed a strike. In the Technical Unit, which consists of 4,000 analysts, designers, and specialists, 71.9% voted to reject the deal and 89.7% approved strike action.

Why Workers Rejected the Offer

Even though Boeing offered the biggest wage pool bump since 1983, workers still voted it down due to clear financial and workplace issues.

  • Inflation Caps: The offer linked pay increases to inflation but capped them at 3%. Members noted this guarantees that their salaries fall behind, given that local Seattle-area inflation was recently benchmarked at 4.5%.
  • Management Mistrust: The bargaining unit councils opposed the offer due to ongoing mistrust over outsourcing, past job losses, and concerns about Boeing's quality and safety issues.

As the next step, union negotiators plan to survey members to determine what changes are required to pass a contract. Since the current contracts do not expire until October 6, 2026, a strike cannot legally begin before that date.

It is worth noting that the current contract negotiations between Boeing and its white-collar workers started on July 1, 2026. This marks the first full contract negotiation between the two parties in nearly 14 years.

Analyst Upgrade Signals Confidence in Boeing's Turnaround

Earlier this month, Argus analyst Kristina Ruggeri upgraded Boeing stock to Buy from Hold with a $265 price target. She said Boeing has strong long‑term prospects thanks to its big role in commercial aerospace and steady defense work. While the company has faced delays, supply issues, and quality concerns in recent years, Ruggeri noted that Boeing has made real progress this year in production, margins, and cash flow.

Ruggeri added that Boeing's cash flow is improving, helped by better manufacturing and a more profitable backlog. The integration of Spirit AeroSystems is moving as planned, which should ease supply chain risk. She said the stock's valuation looks reasonable on price‑to‑sales, and with strong orders and a shift back to positive cash flow, she sees room for near‑term growth.

Is BA a Good Buy Right Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on BA stock based on 17 Buys and one Hold assigned in the past three months. Further, the average Boeing price target of $274.67 per share implies 28.23% upside potential.

data.title: Hims & Hers Health Hit With Visa Penalties as Weight-Loss Complaints Surge
data.description:
Telehealth company Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) is facing penalties from payments giant Visa (V) after customer credit card disputes in its weight-loss subscription business surged beyond acceptable limits. According to Bloomberg, Visa has enrolled HIMS into its Acquirer Monitoring Program following a spike in user complaints and transaction chargebacks in July 2026.

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Each dispute now carries an $8 fee, adding up to nearly $75,000 that will hit the company in September. Visa notified Hims of the enforcement actions through payment processor Stripe earlier in August. To be removed from the monitoring program, Hims must lower its credit card dispute rate below 1.5% of total transactions for three straight months.

According to the report, 75% of Hims' credit card disputes come from its weight‑loss membership. The plan costs $39 for the first month, then $149 after that, with automatic renewals. Hims is now exploring ways to better warn customers about upcoming charges to avoid surprise bills.

A spokesperson for Hims stated that the platform has seen a "relatively small number of disputed charges" and has taken steps to address the issue. The company defended its operations, noting that its checkout process is transparent regarding the cost of memberships and prescriptions for its nearly 3 million customers.

Growing Scrutiny of Hims Billing Practices

The surge in credit card disputes comes at a time of strict regulatory pressure regarding the company's billing practices. In late July 2026, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), alongside authorities in California and Utah, sued Hims & Hers.

The federal lawsuit alleges that the company engaged in deceptive billing, such as charging consumers before they spoke to medical professionals and purposely making recurring subscriptions difficult to cancel.

Also, some customers have raised concerns that the company makes cancellation difficult and continues charging their cards afterward.

With the FTC already suing the company, the Visa warning adds fresh pressure on one of Hims' fastest‑growing businesses. This shows that its subscription model may need clearer communication as it grows.

Turning to Wall Street, HIMS stock has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on three Buys and eight Holds assigned in the past three months. The average price target for Hims & Hers is $33.25, implying a 1.57% downside risk from the current price.
